title: [Chapitre] VIII. Analysis situs (quatrième mouture) : notes manuscrites (26/06-04/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting, from the surrounding pages: L is a totally ordered set of 'vertices'. M is the set of cells of the corresponding 1-dimensional cellular line. There are point cells P_a (a in L) and open segment cells S_ab (a<b). For a part Φ of M, δΦ is the set of vertices involved, ∂Φ its boundary, and or(δΦ), ex(δΦ) are its smallest ('origine') and largest ('extrémité') vertices.

The previous page defines X <_pos Y ('X lies to the left of Y') by four cases:
- P_x < P_y if x<y;
- P_x < S_ab if x ≤ a;
- S_ab < P_y if b ≤ y;
- S_ab < S_a'b' if b ≤ a'.

Read geometrically, points are closed singletons and segments are open intervals. Then X <_pos Y says exactly that X lies entirely to the left of Y.

This page first records a summary. One has found an order relation on M whose comparability relation is the disposition relation X|·|Y: X|·|Y ⇔ X <_pos Y or Y <_pos X. In modern terms, the disjointness graph of these cells is the comparability graph of an interval order.

The order is then lifted to arbitrary parts: Φ <_pos Ψ :⇔ X <_pos Y for all X∈Φ and Y∈Ψ.

A margin NB (heavily corrected) analyses what Φ <_pos Ψ implies:
- δΦ ∩ δΨ is either empty or a single vertex α = ex(δΦ) = or(δΨ);
- in the latter case P_α cannot belong to both Φ and Ψ.

For admissible (connected pre-form) parts, a stronger relation Φ <!_pos Ψ is introduced. It requires Φ <_pos Ψ and, when ex Φ = or Ψ = a, also P_a ∉ Φ and P_a ∉ Ψ. The drawing shows two segments abutting at a common point a. If P_a belonged to one of them, Φ∪Ψ would be connected; this is the 'recollé' case that the next page explicitly excludes. The relation therefore expresses that Φ and Ψ are open-and-closed in Φ∪Ψ, i.e. separate connected components placed left to right.

Purpose, as the next page shows: an arbitrary pre-form is classified as a flag (strictly increasing chain for <!_pos) of connected pre-forms. These are its connected components, linearly ordered along the line. This is a step in a purely combinatorial description of 'tame' subsets of a stratified 1-dimensional space within Grothendieck's 1986 'Analysis situs' project.
errors: The definition of Φ <_pos Ψ writes 'X < Y' without the subscript pos. Grothendieck himself warns (previous page) that the subscript is essential to avoid confusion with the other order <, ≤ on M.
The condition rendered 'R × Φ = or Ψ' should almost certainly read 'ex Φ = or Ψ' (extremity of Φ equals origin of Ψ).

In the margin NB the first attempts are struck out. The surviving statement 'δΦ ∩ δΨ = ∅, et si α ∈ δΦ ∩ δΨ ...' is self-contradictory as written. The intended statement is: either δΦ∩δΨ = ∅, or δΦ∩δΨ = {α} with α = ex(δΦ) = or(δΨ) and P_α ∉ Φ∩Ψ.

The characterization on the previous page, 'X <_pos Y ⇔ X‖Y et or(δX) < ex(δY)', looks inverted. From the four cases it should be ex(δX) ≤ or(δY), plus disjointness. This is not on this page, but this page relies on it.

ideas.what: Disjointness of the cells of a 1-dimensional cell decomposition of a line is exactly the comparability relation of the 'lies to the left of' order
ideas.modern_name: Interval order; the disjointness graph of intervals is the comparability graph of an interval order

ideas.what: Order on parts, Φ <_pos Ψ iff elementwise X <_pos Y
ideas.modern_name: Lifting a strict order to subsets (set-wise precedence)

ideas.what: Strict precedence <!_pos excluding gluing at a shared endpoint point-cell, so that Φ and Ψ are clopen in Φ∪Ψ; used to describe a pre-form as a flag of its connected components
ideas.modern_name: Decomposition of a subcomplex / constructible subset of a 1-dimensional stratified space into linearly ordered connected components
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore (o-minimal cell decomposition in dimension 1, van den Dries et al.)
ideas.where_published: The general programme of 'topologie modérée' is in Esquisse d'un programme (1984); this specific combinatorics is not published as far as I know

deep.surprise_reason: The page is elementary bookkeeping in Grothendieck's combinatorial 1-dimensional analysis situs. It sets up an interval order on cells and a separated-precedence relation, used to decompose pre-forms into ordered connected components. The ideas are correct and standard. Only the context (his 1986 tame-topology project) is of historical interest.
transcription_corrections: 'disposition [..] croisée[?]' — the word is unclear in the image. Mathematically the relation X|·|Y is disjointness of cells, so 'disjointe' or similar is likely intended rather than 'croisée'.
'$X < Y$' in the definition of Φ <_pos Ψ: the subscript pos is implied.
'NB Si Φ, Ψ des parfaits[?] quelconques' should read 'des parties quelconques'.
'R × Φ = or Ψ' should read 'ex Φ = or Ψ'.
Margin: the struck-out line reads '[δΦ ∩ δΨ = {a} et P_a ∉ Φ ∩ Ψ]'. The surviving intended content is 'δΦ∩δΨ = ∅ ou {α}, α = ex(δΦ) = or(δΨ), et P_α ∉ Φ∩Ψ'.
Margin top: 'partie quelconques' (with Φ ≤_pos Ψ) rather than 'parfaits'.
The drawing shows two arcs labelled Φ and Ψ meeting at a marked point (·), with the variant 'ou l'inverse' shown next to it.
'[...] comme[?] des positions de M_0 ⊂ M' is plausibly '...les parties de M ... comme des parties de M_0 ⊂ M'. The left margin attempts 'ou si α = ex... M_0 ⊂ M' are interleaved with it.
